prompt: When BOTH an electric and a magnetic field are present, the force on a moving charge is:

options.text: F = q(E + v cross B)
F = qE only, since magnetic fields do no work
F = qvB sin θ only
F = q(E cross B)
F = qE times qvB

explanation: The two contributions simply add: the electric part qE, which acts whether or not the charge is moving, plus the magnetic part qv cross B, which needs motion. Note that the magnetic part doing no WORK does not mean it exerts no FORCE: it steers without changing the speed.

why.a: Correct, and this is the full Lorentz force.
why.b: Wrong. Doing no work is not the same as exerting no force; a magnetic force bends the path.
why.c: Wrong. That drops the electric contribution entirely.
why.d: Wrong. E and B are not crossed with each other here. That combination is the Poynting vector, a different quantity.
why.e: Wrong. Forces add; they do not multiply.

prompt: The cyclotron frequency is f = qB over 2 π m. A proton is injected twice into the same field, the second time at double the speed. What happens to its frequency of revolution?

options.text: Unchanged, because there is no v in the formula
It doubles
It halves
It quadruples
It falls by the square root of two

explanation: There is no v in f = qB over 2 π m, so the frequency is independent of speed, and so is the period T = 2 π m over qB. A faster proton simply travels a wider circle, since r = mv over qB, and covers that longer path in exactly the same time. That is the cyclotron principle: it is what allows a fixed-frequency accelerating voltage to keep pushing particles that are getting faster.

why.a: Correct, and the absence of v from the formula is the whole point.
why.b: Wrong. Doubling the speed doubles the RADIUS, not the frequency.
why.d: Wrong. No quantity here scales as a square.
why.e: Wrong. No square root appears in this relationship.

topic: the period of the circular motion
prompt: The period of a charge circling in a magnetic field is T = 2 π m over qB, which like the frequency is independent of the {{1}}.
explanation: The speed. Mass, charge and field all appear in the formula and all change the period; speed does not appear and does not. It matters for the helical path, where the pitch is v cos θ times T: the period is fixed by the field and the particle, and only the along-field velocity decides how far it advances in that time.

prompt: A straight wire of length L carries current I in a magnetic field B. The force on it is F = BIL sin θ. At what angle is this force greatest?

options.text: 90 degrees, with the wire across the field
0 degrees, with the wire along the field
45 degrees
180 degrees
The angle makes no difference

explanation: sin 90 = 1, the largest the sine can be, so the force is maximum with the wire perpendicular to the field. Along the field, sin 0 = 0 and the wire feels nothing at all, which is the same rule as for a single moving charge: only the component of motion ACROSS the field is deflected.

why.b: Wrong, and it is the ZERO-force case.
why.c: Wrong. sin 45 is about 0.71, so substantial but not maximal.
why.d: Wrong. sin 180 = 0, so no force, same as along the field.
why.e: Wrong. The sine factor is precisely the angle's effect.

prompt: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is m = NIA, where N is the number of turns, I the current and A the {{1}} the loop encloses.
explanation: The area, in square metres, giving m the unit A m squared. Test 2 question 7 works it backwards, giving a torque and asking for m. Note that the m here is a MAGNETIC MOMENT and not the mass that appears in r = mv over qB, which is the most confusable pair of symbols in the topic.

prompt: The torque on a current loop is τ = mB sin θ = NIAB sin θ. When is it zero?

options.text: When the magnetic moment m lies along B
When m is perpendicular to B
When the current is at its maximum
Only when the current is zero
When the loop has more than one turn

explanation: sin 0 = 0, so aligned means no torque. It is the exact counterpart of the ELECTRIC dipole, whose torque pE sin θ also vanishes on alignment. Both are the position the field is trying to turn the object into, which is why a compass needle settles pointing along the field and then stops.

why.a: Correct, and it is the stable resting position.
why.b: Wrong. Perpendicular is where the torque is at its MAXIMUM.
why.c: Wrong. More current gives more torque, not less.
why.d: Wrong. Zero current is one way, but alignment gives zero torque with the current still flowing.
why.e: Wrong. More turns increase the torque.

prompt: The cyclotron frequency is the number of revolutions per second of a charge in a magnetic field, and it is independent of the particle's speed.
explanation: True on both counts. f = qB over 2 π m contains the charge, the field and the mass, and nothing about how fast the particle is going. A faster particle circles on a wider radius and arrives back at the same moment.

why.true: Correct. Revolutions per second, and speed does not enter it.
why.false: Wrong. Look at the formula: there is no v in f = qB over 2 π m.

prompt: Magnetic flux density, the quantity everyone simply calls the magnetic field, is measured in {{1}}.
explanation: The tesla, symbol T. Keep it apart from the weber, which is the unit of magnetic FLUX rather than flux density, and one weber is one tesla square metre. A tesla is a large unit: the fields in this course run from 0.03 T up to 0.6 T, and a fridge magnet is only a few thousandths.
